config.name: g1-enum-fixed-remeasure
config.description:
Re-measure G2 (Joules per VALID output) now that the prompt/schema enum contradiction is fixed. NIGHT-REPORT §4 left this decision to the Linux side; the decision taken is FIX THE ASSET, not case-normalise the validator, because the schema is the contract and a prompt whose own worked example violates it is simply a bug.
What changed in the repo before this run (commit alongside this config): examples/desktop/prompts/constant_data{,_en}.txt lines 70 and 73 showed "status": "INCOMPLETE" while MedScreeningInputStatus admits only ['incomplete','complete','skipped'] — the enum member NAMES are uppercase but their VALUES are lowercase, and JSON Schema validates values. Both files now say "incomplete". g1_mask_cost_pilot.py:485 reads constant_data_en.txt as the system prompt, so this asset is exactly what the model was copying.
WHY THIS MATTERS: in 002 the unconstrained condition scored 1% valid, and 89 of its 99 failures were enum rejections with the model emitting INCOMPLETE ×47 and COMPLETE ×38 — faithfully copying the prompt. The grammar conditions could not emit uppercase by construction, so they were immune. The resulting 100x J-per-valid gap therefore measured "constrained decoding masks a prompt bug", NOT "unconstrained decoding produces invalid tool calls". This run separates those two claims for the first time.
COMPARABILITY WARNING for whoever analyses this: results here are NOT directly comparable to 002/003 validity or J-per-valid numbers. The system prompt changed. Latency and energy rows remain comparable (the prompt is the same length to within a few characters and the sampler settings are identical).
Models: the two that failed 002/003 on the enum bug specifically. qwen3 is excluded here because its failure mode was truncation, not the enum — that is experiment 006's job.
Expected reading: if unconstrained validity jumps from ~1% to something high, the 002 headline was an asset artifact and G2's claim must be restated. If it stays low with a DIFFERENT failure-mode breakdown, that breakdown is the real G2 finding. Either outcome is publishable; conflating them was not.
